title: Learning while it sleeps
blurb: After a day of practice, the model studies what it found and settles it in. Here is how a night of sleep works, what it scored, and what is not shown.

scenes.heading: Where we are: outside the five parts

caption.text: Sleep is not a sixth part. It is a way of learning, tested so far only in research.
After a day of practice, the model studies what it found and settles it in.
The model runs its own night. The tests used six starting copies from an earlier design.

scenes.heading: A puzzle with a hidden rule

caption.text: A few examples hide a rule: 2 gives 5, 4 gives 9, 7 gives 15.
The model tries rules. A try counts only if it fits every example, so no answer key is needed.
Only x times 2 plus 1 fits all three. So 10 gives 21 (our arithmetic: 10 times 2, plus 1).

scenes.heading: What the test really is

caption.text: The test has five kinds of rules, 65 rules in all, as the project's notes describe it.
The model reads which rule a few new examples show, then answers a new question of that kind on the first try.
It is not inventing a rule it has never met.
The notes do not agree on whether these rules were practised before. That is not settled.

scenes.heading: Where it started, and the old sleep

caption.text: At the start, the model scored 41.6 out of 100 on this test, as the project's notes say.
The old sleep lifted that to 71.3, give or take 2.5, averaged over six copies.
It needed 558 to 610 updates, by its formula. One update is one small nudge to every setting.
By kind, a×x+b was hardest at 15.5, and x squared easiest at 98.7.

scenes.heading: One night of the new sleep

caption.text: The model runs its own night: its own tries, at a temperature it picks, plus chain search.
Then it sleeps for 256 updates, each of 1,024 rows. A row is one practice question.
Half the rows are fresh dreams, new questions written from a found program, so none is read twice. Half are fresh skills rows.
Every 32 updates it checks its fit rate on 128 held questions and keeps its best saved model.

'A row is one practice question' and 'fit rate' are plain-words readings of PR #53 wording; 'fit' = how often its tries fit the examples (creative-roadmap-page.html:251). scenes.heading: The pass marks: four met, one not shown

caption.text: Every pass mark was fixed before the run. Score: 76.1, where 71.3 was needed.
Updates: 256 each night, under half of the old sleep's.
Harm measure: did old skills drop? No. Old skills also went up, with a likely range above zero.
Last: does sleep beat plain practice? That was not shown.

src: animations/model-explainer-build/sources/pr-53-consolidation-sleep.md:4 (every pass mark fixed before its run), :7-12 (verdict table)
scenes.notes: Numbers in square brackets are likely ranges. Mark 3 'no harm vs the pre-sleep model (harm_measure)': in_dist +0.12 to +0.82, no family fires on any parent. 'Through transfer' = sleep minus replay-only control, must be above 0.

scenes.heading: Old skills: no harm, but who gets the credit?

caption.text: Harm measure: did old skills get worse? On every copy they moved +0.12 to +0.82 points.
Pooled over the six copies, they rose by 0.52, likely range 0.31 to 0.74.
A replay-only control, practising the same skills rows, raised them by 2.11, range 1.88 to 2.32.
So the gain is not shown to come from the sleep. Sleep minus control: −1.58.

scenes.heading: Fresh dreams or re-read rows?

caption.text: The old sleep re-reads the day's rows. The new one writes a fresh dream each time, so no row is read twice.
At equal updates, fresh dreams beat re-read rows by 7.4 (range 3.5 to 11.3) and 5.5 (range 0.8 to 10.2).
Two copies, development questions only. Whether fresh dreams cut harm could not be tested: re-read rows did no harm either.

scenes.heading: What is not shown

caption.text: 71.3 is the old sleep's stored number, from its own near-copy starting copies. It is not side by side with 76.1.
Each copy slept once, so a repeat might score differently.
The stop rule never ended a night early. Only keeping the best saved model acted.
Building the copies cost rule-from-examples skills 2.3 points. Sleep won back about 0.5; the control, most.
Against the earlier model, the harm check still fails on all six copies. Report only.

scenes.heading: Follow-ups, all on hold

caption.text: Next, sleeps where the model picks its own replay rows. SC kept its gain but failed the harm mark.
On SC, 2 to 3 skill groups fell 6.5 to 11.0 points per copy. SCL, with a slower learning rate, passed its marks.
Both ran on two other copies, not the six. All of this is on hold; none feeds the first big training run.

scenes.heading: Another test: sleeping on its own tries

caption.text: A different test, from Oct 7: first answer right out of 100, on 5 new rules and 256 development questions.
Before sleeping: 0.4 for copy A, 1.2 for copy B. Sleeping on tries that failed the check did nothing.
Sleeping on tries that passed the check: 27.3 and 35.9. The line, set first, was 15 more than before.
Two copies, one short sleep each. Not comparable with 76.1 or 71.3.

scenes.heading: What to remember

caption.text: Sleep is a night of study after a day of practice. The new sleep scored 76.1 in 256 updates, not in a paired test.
Old skills were not harmed, but sleep is not shown to help them more than plain practice.
A research result, not yet part of the model. The first big run does not wait for it; a finished model needs it.
